Q: IOS application Distribution without appstore A:

If you want to distribute an app between people, the only way is become an Apple Developer Program member. Then you can use one of the way, Unlisted app distribution, for example.

Q: "String iterator not dereferncable" with boost async_read_some A:

I had a similar problem, some of ASIO's read/write functions takes references to mutable buffers that you provide and require that the buffer is persistent until the async function is complete. Using a string as a character buffer for example passing asio::buffer(std::string("data")) would result in this assert because the string is out of scope by the time asio processes the async function. That said, look through all your read/write functions and ensure where you pass a string as a mutable buffer, the string is persistent.

Q: HTML slide - PPTX slide conversion using the pptx gen js A:

It would make sense to provide a simple MRE of the sorts of things that go wrong with images of before and after and a table of coordinates of objects that have been misplaced. It may be possible to make an educated guess about the flaws from how things move around.

If you want to do any better than PptxGenJS you may have to write something from scratch.

Fighting with MS Office code you are always up against WYS is never quite WYG (so the fault(s) could be at either end of the process chain).

Q: GitLab CI: How to print an error message and exit? A:

The issue isn’t the print, but your script terminating before you get to the print. In the case of gitlab CI, and any scripts that sets -e as an option, any command returning non-zero will terminate the script.

The return status of a pipe is it’s last command. If you can use $? on it, then you can use it in the if directly, where the return value is consumed by the if and does not terminate the script:

if ! echo -n "${CI_COMMIT_TAG}" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-(alpha|beta|rc|ALPHA|BETA|RC)[0-9]*)?$'; then
  >&2 echo "Invalid release TAG: ${CI_COMMIT_TAG}"
  exit 1
fi

Otherwise the standard way to ignore a return status is to or it with the bash no-op statement :, this will hide the non-zero return value from the top script:

echo -n "${CI_COMMIT_TAG}" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-(alpha|beta|rc|ALPHA|BETA|RC)[0-9]*)?$' || :

But then you lose the return value that you wanted to test. You can however use that technique to print something, and the or-d print will hide the return value as well:

check=$(echo -n "${CI_COMMIT_TAG}" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-(alpha|beta|rc|ALPHA|BETA|RC)[0-9]*)?$' && echo ok || echo no)
if [ "$check" -ne ok ]; then
  >&2 echo "Invalid release TAG: ${CI_COMMIT_TAG}"
  exit 1
fi

Q: GTK: How can I fix this problem: Could not load a pixbuf from /org/gtk/libgtk/icons/16x16/status/image-missing.png A:

Well, this is almost five years old, but it could use an answer.

It is helpful to look at other applications that install GTK and see what they include (e.g. Inkscape).

You are probably missing the GDK loader libraries.

For my application, I also install:

.../lib/gdk-pixbuf-2.0
.../lib/girepository-1.0
.../etc/gtk-3.0/im-multipress.conf
.../share/glib-2.0/schemas
.../etc/fonts
.../share/gtk-3.0/3.0.0/immodules
.../share/locale/*/glib20.mo 
.../share/locale/*/gtk30.mo 
.../bin/gdbus.exe
.../bin/gspawn-win64-helper-console.exe
.../bin/gspawn-win64-helper.exe

Some applications (e.g. Inkscape) muck with the windows path, and your application will pick up the incorrect set of GTK libraries. Try installing your application, then Inkscape, and make sure both your application and Inkscape work. And vice-versa.

I use a launcher to set the path for my application and avoid any changes to the general Windows path. Then I don't need to worry about what other applications are doing.
